name: alarm-cadence

description.en: W-LOOP: a venue's Durable Object alarm runs its timed work (outbox drain, till-link poll, fiscal) IN ITS OWN TURN -- no runner object, no reads back (11.9 -> 1 object request per firing, counted in memory: 11 -> 1). The till link polls only inside the venue's opening hours, or the storefront's 11:00-23:00 when none are filed (no longer 'always open'), backing off 1 -> 2 -> 5 -> 15 min while nothing new arrives; an idle linked venue went from 1,440 alarms a day to 76 (in memory). The nightly cron makes ONE request to the platform object, which fans the night out to the venues FAN_BATCH (25) per alarm turn; each venue runs its own night (retention, prunes, chain + witness, rotation, backup) in its own alarm.
description.uk: Будильник закладу виконує роботу у власному ході (без runner-об'єкта), каса опитується лише в години роботи з паузами 1-2-5-15 хв, а нічний cron робить один запит, і кожен заклад проходить ніч у власному будильнику.

producer.what: timer_alarm_in(): the venue's jobs in its own alarm turn, with an Env that answers its own name in process (edge::Own)
nightly(): the cron's ONE request to the platform object (/fold/timer?fan=1)
night_fan(): FAN_BATCH venues pinged per platform alarm turn (/fold/timer?night=1)

consumer.what: the till-link sheet's 'Polling' row (eb_cadence / eb_cadenceNow, sq/en/uk/ru), tour anchor ebills.cadence
Cloudflare's own count of alarms per object and of the scheduled run

transport.auth: none: Durable Object binding, not reachable from the internet

transport.who: the platform object's alarm -> each venue's object

limits_cited.quote: A subrequest is any request a Worker makes using the Fetch API or to Cloudflare services like R2 , KV , or D1 . ... Subrequests per invocation: Workers Free 50 ... Subrequests to internal services: 1,000
limits_cited.consequence: R2/KV/D1 calls DO count; Durable Object stub calls are not named on the page (hypothesis: the 1,000 internal-services counter). The old nightly spent >= 4-6 of them per venue in one invocation; the new cron spends 1.
